files.purpose: New in 1.6.2: a @MainActor enum TerminalFont whose single public entry point preferred(fallbackSize:) picks the NSFont the embedded SwiftTerm view draws with, so that a Starship or powerline prompt's Nerd Font icons render instead of empty boxes. It reads the font the user configured in Ghostty (plain-text config), iTerm2 (defaults 'New Bookmarks' / 'Normal Font') and Terminal.app (archived NSFont in the default profile), ordering running terminals first, then prefers a configured font that covers four Nerd Font probe glyphs, else that font's installed Nerd Font sibling family, else any installed family whose name contains 'nerd font', else the configured font itself, and finally the monospaced system font.
key_symbols: @MainActor enum TerminalFont
static func preferred(fallbackSize: CGFloat = 12) -> NSFont
private static func configuredFonts() -> [NSFont]
private static func ghosttyFont() -> NSFont?
private static var ghosttyConfigURLs: [URL]
private static func terminalFont() -> NSFont?
private static func iTermFont() -> NSFont?
private static let nerdProbes: [UnicodeScalar] = [UInt32(0xE0B0), UInt32(0xE0B6), UInt32(0xF015), UInt32(0xF0035)].compactMap(UnicodeScalar.init)
private static func hasNerdGlyphs(_ font: NSFont) -> Bool
private static func nerdSibling(of font: NSFont) -> NSFont?
private static func firstInstalledNerdFont(size: CGFloat) -> NSFont?
private static func resolve(_ name: String, size: CGFloat) -> NSFont?
private static func normalized(_ name: String) -> String
calls_into: Called by TerminalSession.init in TerminalStore.swift line 22 (view.font = TerminalFont.preferred())
state_owned: None mutable. Only the static constant nerdProbes; every call re-reads configs, running apps and installed families (no caching).
side_effects: Reads two Ghostty config files from disk, the Terminal.app and iTerm2 preference domains, and the list of running applications, on every preferred() call. preferred() runs from TerminalSession.init (TerminalStore.swift line 22), so it runs for every TerminalSession constructed: each open()/run()/ensureTerminal() tab AND every TerminalStore.restart(_:), which builds a fresh `TerminalSession(...)` (TerminalStore.swift lines 142-147). A configured font that changed since the tab was first opened therefore changes a restarted tab's font and size. No writes.
platform_assumptions: AppKit NSFont / NSFontManager / NSWorkspace / NSKeyedUnarchiver; a Windows port needs a DirectWrite or system font enumeration and glyph-coverage check instead of coveredCharacterSet.

macOS terminal apps and their bundle IDs "com.mitchellh.ghostty", "com.googlecode.iterm2", "com.apple.Terminal"; on Windows the equivalent sources would be Windows Terminal settings.json and others, which this file does not cover.
macOS paths "Library/Application Support/com.mitchellh.ghostty/config" and XDG ".config/ghostty/config" under the home directory.
CFPreferences-backed UserDefaults suites of other apps (Terminal.app 'Window Settings', iTerm2 'New Bookmarks').
NSFont(name:) accepting a family name (used with family names from availableFontFamilies) as well as PostScript names.
persisted_fields: Reads, never writes. Ghostty config keys: "font-family" (FIRST occurrence wins: `case "font-family" where name == nil:`; comma list allowed, first entry taken, spaces and double quotes trimmed) and "font-size" (`case "font-size": if let points = Double(value), points > 0 { size = CGFloat(points) }` has no such guard, so it runs on every matching line and the LAST valid font-size in the file wins; default 12 when absent).
Terminal.app domain com.apple.Terminal: "Default Window Settings" (profile name, default "Basic"), "Window Settings" dictionary, the profile entry's "Font" (Data, archived NSFont).

iTerm2 domain com.googlecode.iterm2: "New Bookmarks" array of dictionaries, each "Normal Font" string formatted as PostScript name, a space, then the size (e.g. last space-separated token parsed as Double).
ui_elements: No UI. Default fallback size 12 pt; final fallback NSFont.monospacedSystemFont(ofSize: 12, weight: .regular).
feature_notes: preferred(): configured = configuredFonts(); returns the first configured font where hasNerdGlyphs is true; otherwise, if any configured font exists, returns nerdSibling(of: first) ?? firstInstalledNerdFont(size: first.pointSize) ?? first; with no configured font returns firstInstalledNerdFont(size: fallbackSize) ?? monospacedSystemFont(ofSize: fallbackSize, weight: .regular).

configuredFonts(): readers in fixed order ghostty, iTerm2, Terminal; the running ones (by bundle identifier) come first in that order, then the non-running ones; compactMap calls every reader, so all three sources are read each time.

Ghostty parse: per file, lines trimmed of whitespace, lines starting with "#" and lines without "=" skipped, key and value split at the first "=" and trimmed. size resets to 12 for each file. The first file that yields a non-empty name that resolve() can turn into a font wins; otherwise the second file is tried; otherwise nil.

Ghostty comment handling: only whole lines whose trimmed text starts with "#" are skipped (line 41 `guard !line.hasPrefix("#"), let equal = line.firstIndex(of: "=") else { continue }`). A trailing comment stays in the value: `font-size = 14 # big` gives the value "14 # big", `Double(value)` is nil, and the size is silently left at its previous value (12 by default). The same trailing text would stay in a font-family value, since only spaces and double quotes are trimmed from it.
Ghostty config URL order: home + "Library/Application Support/com.mitchellh.ghostty/config", then home + ".config/ghostty/config".

iTermFont iterates every bookmark in array order (it does not look up the default profile GUID) and returns the first whose "Normal Font" parses to a size and for which `NSFont(name: parts.dropLast().joined(separator: " "), size: CGFloat(size))` (line 87) is non-nil. This is a DIRECT NSFont(name:size:) call, not the resolve() helper: unlike ghosttyFont (line 55 `resolve(name, size: size)`), there is no fallback to a normalized family-name match, so a name that is not an exact PostScript or family name gives nil for that bookmark and the loop moves on to the next.
terminalFont uses profile = defaults "Default Window Settings" ?? "Basic" and returns nil if 'Window Settings', the profile entry or its 'Font' Data is missing, or if unarchiving fails.

Nerd probes (line 96): U+E0B0, U+E0B6, U+F015, U+F0035, built with `.compactMap(UnicodeScalar.init)`; hasNerdGlyphs requires all four to be in coveredCharacterSet (`nerdProbes.allSatisfy { covered.contains($0) }`). The file's own comment (lines 94-95) groups them as "a powerline cap, two Font Awesome marks and a Material one from the supplementary plane"; that is the source's description (so it counts one powerline cap, not two). Which Nerd Font range each code point belongs to is not stated beyond that comment.
normalized(name): lowercased, spaces and "-" removed, then "nerdfont" replaced by "nf" (so "GeistMono Nerd Font" and "Geist Mono NF" both become "geistmononf").

nerdSibling(of:): target = normalized(familyName) + "nf"; first installed family whose normalized name equals target, opened at the same point size. A family that is already a Nerd Font variant yields a target ending in "nfnf" and finds nothing.
firstInstalledNerdFont(size:): first family in availableFontFamilies whose name localizedCaseInsensitiveContains "nerd font".
resolve(name:size:): NSFont(name:size:) first; else the first installed family whose normalized name equals normalized(name).

B1->B2: added in 1.6.2 (the whole 138-line file is new; diff shows 138 insertions). TerminalStore.swift switched from NSFont.monospacedSystemFont(ofSize: 12, weight: .regular) to TerminalFont.preferred() in the same release.
unresolved_questions: Which Windows sources (Windows Terminal settings.json profiles.defaults.font.face/size, per-profile fonts, WezTerm, Alacritty) the port should read to reach parity in spirit, since none of the three macOS sources exist on Windows.
Whether NSFont(name:) resolving a family name (rather than a PostScript name) picks the Regular face on every family; the file relies on it but does not say.

files.purpose: TerminalPanel is the per-thread terminal drawer shown at the bottom of a conversation: a 38 pt tab row of TerminalTab capsules with a plus button and a hide chevron, the selected session's SwiftTerm view hosted through TerminalHost, an empty state with a 'New shell' button, and a resize strip on the top edge that clamps the dragged drawer height to 140-760 points (the stored height itself is drawn unclamped) and commits it to settings only on release. The file also defines the AppKit resize grip view with its hover-grown bar, the NSViewRepresentable host that moves the long-lived terminal view between containers and installs an Escape-at-prompt key monitor, and TerminalHostContainer, which parks autoresizing during a live window resize and re-syncs the frame at most every 50 ms so SwiftTerm does not re-wrap every frame.

Installs a process-wide local keyDown monitor per hosted terminal; swallows Escape (returns nil) when the shell owns the foreground, and calls onEscapeAtPrompt which sets runtime.isTerminalVisible = false.

NSWindow live-resize notifications and inLiveResize; autoresizingMask [.width, .height].

Coordinate system with y increasing upward (locationInWindow.y delta positive upward grows the drawer); a top-left origin system must invert the sign.

persisted_fields: settings.terminalHeight (Double, points): written once on drag release (onEnd, `if let dragHeight { model.settings.terminalHeight = dragHeight }`) with the drag value min(760, max(140, origin + delta)). Only the drag value is clamped: the drawer is drawn at `.frame(height: dragHeight ?? model.settings.terminalHeight)` (line 80) with no clamp, so a stored value outside 140-760 is drawn as is until the next drag. Because mouseUp always sends a final onChange, even a click on the strip with no movement writes the clamped stored value back. Its default lives in AppSettings, not in this file.
ui_elements: Tab row: HStack spacing 6, horizontal ScrollView(.horizontal, showsIndicators: false) holding tabs in HStack spacing 4, with `.fixedSize(horizontal: false, vertical: true)` on the ScrollView (line 34); row padding horizontal 10, height 38.
Plus button: Image "plus" in Chrome.iconFont, .buttonStyle(.chip), help and accessibility label "New terminal"; action `terminals.open(threadID: runtime.threadID, directory: directory)` (line 36).

Hide button: Image "chevron.down" in Chrome.iconFont, .chip, help "Hide terminal" + ShortcutStore.hint(for: .toggleTerminal), accessibility label "Hide terminal"; action `runtime.isTerminalVisible = false` (line 46). A Spacer(minLength: 0) sits between plus and hide. TerminalHost's doc comment (lines 320-321) says Escape at the prompt closes the panel "the way ⌘J closes it", i.e. the source names Cmd+J as the terminal toggle; the binding itself (.toggleTerminal) is defined in ShortcutStore, not in this file.

Empty state: VStack spacing 10, Text "No shell open in this thread" in .system(.body) Chrome.secondaryText, Button "New shell" .glass .controlSize(.small) with action `terminals.open(threadID: runtime.threadID, directory: directory)`, frame maxWidth/maxHeight infinity.
Panel height `dragHeight ?? model.settings.terminalHeight` (unclamped when not dragging; the 140/760 bounds apply only to dragHeight); resize strip overlay at top with height 8.
Background: UnevenRoundedRectangle top corners Chrome.sheetCornerRadius, continuous, fill Color(white: 0.08) dark / Color(white: 0.985) light.

Resize grip: CALayer bar height 2.5, corner radius 1.25, width 12 at rest and 28 when hovered or dragging, opacity 0 at rest and 0.6 when shown, colour NSColor.labelColor, centred; animated 0.18 s easeOut; cursor resizeUpDown over the whole strip. Tracking area options `[.mouseEnteredAndExited, .activeAlways, .inVisibleRect]` (line 242): .activeAlways means the hover-grown grip appears even when the window is not key. acceptsFirstMouse returns true and mouseDownCanMoveWindow is false.

TerminalTab: HStack spacing 6: Image "terminal" .caption; Text(session.title) lineLimit 1; when not running an "arrow.clockwise" button (.caption2 bold, plain, Chrome.secondaryText, help "Start a new shell in this tab", accessibility "Restart <title>"); an "xmark" button (.caption2 bold, plain, Chrome.secondaryText, opacity 1 when hovering or selected else 0, hit testing only then, help "Close terminal", accessibility "Close <title>").

TerminalTab styling: font .callout, padding horizontal 10 vertical 5, foreground .primary when selected else .secondary, capsule background .primary.opacity(0.08) when selected else clear, `.contentShape(.capsule)` so the whole capsule is the tap target of `.onTapGesture(perform: select)`, .onHover sets isHovering, opacity 0.55 when the shell has exited, help session.title or "<title> · the shell has exited", `.accessibilityElement(children: .contain)` (the restart and close buttons stay separate accessibility children), accessibility label title or "<title>, the shell has exited", traits .isButton plus .isSelected when selected.
feature_notes: Tab tap sets terminals.selection[runtime.threadID] = session.id; restart and close go to the store.

Drag: onBegin stores dragOrigin = settings.terminalHeight and sets isTerminalResizing; onChange sets dragHeight = min(760, max(140, origin + delta)) where delta = event.locationInWindow.y - pressOriginY (positive upward); onEnd writes dragHeight to settings if set, clears both, clears isTerminalResizing. mouseUp sends one final onChange before onEnd.
The drag strip is only the top 8 pt overlay, not the whole tab row, so sideways drags over tabs scroll them (comment lines 81-83).

Escape handling: keyCode 53, no modifiers within KeyChord.allowedModifiers, the event window's firstResponder is the terminal view, and TerminalSession.foregroundJobIsTheShell(view.process.shellPid) is true; then onEscapeAtPrompt() runs and the event is consumed. Otherwise the event passes through (vim, claude, less keep Escape).

updateNSView: applyAppearance(isDark:), re-attach if the view's superview is not this container, set hostedView, then if runtime.terminalWantsFocus, in a main-actor Task re-check it and the view's window, set it false and makeFirstResponder(view).
attach(to:): removeFromSuperview, frame = container.bounds, autoresizingMask [.width, .height], addSubview, applyAppearance, hostedView = view.

Live resize: willStartLiveResize sets hostedView.autoresizingMask = []; resizeSubviews during inLiveResize schedules one syncFrame 50 ms later unless one is pending; didEndLiveResize cancels pending, restores [.width, .height] and syncs. syncFrame only writes when bounds are non-zero and differ from the view's frame and the view is still a subview of this container.

B1->B2: four edits. (1) Empty-state text font .system(size: 13) became .system(.body). (2) and (3) the restart and close buttons in TerminalTab changed .foregroundStyle(.secondary) to .foregroundStyle(Chrome.secondaryText). (4) The two live-resize NotificationCenter closures now wrap their bodies in MainActor.assumeIsolated { ... } (self?.hostedView?.autoresizingMask = [] and self?.finishResize()). No geometry or behaviour numbers changed.
unresolved_questions: The value of Chrome.sheetCornerRadius, Chrome.iconFont, the .chip button style and the default settings.terminalHeight are defined elsewhere and must be taken from those files.
KeyChord.allowedModifiers membership is defined elsewhere; it decides which modified Escapes still close the drawer.

files.purpose: TerminalStore.swift holds the model side of the embedded terminal: TerminalSession wraps one SwiftTerm LocalProcessTerminalView running the user's login shell in a pseudo terminal with Droppy-specific environment variables, applies theme colours only when the appearance changes, and can tell through sysctl whether the shell owns the terminal foreground. TerminalStore is the @Observable per-thread registry of sessions and the selected session, with open, run-script, ensure, restart-in-place, close, close-all and terminate-all operations; a private TerminalBridge delegate marks a session not running when its process exits.

Darwin sysctl with CTL_KERN, KERN_PROC, KERN_PROC_PID and kinfo_proc.kp_eproc.e_tpgid / e_pgid
state_owned: TerminalSession: id, threadID, directory, title, isRunning, view, bridge, appliedDark.
TerminalStore: sessions keyed by thread UUID (ordered arrays), selection keyed by thread UUID to session UUID. In memory only.
side_effects: TerminalSession.init spawns the user's shell as a login shell in a pty in the given directory.

terminate() is `guard isRunning else { return }; view.terminate(); isRunning = false` (lines 59-63): it kills the process through SwiftTerm only while isRunning is true, and is a no-op once the shell has already exited (processEnded() set isRunning = false). close(), restart(), closeAll and terminateAll all call it, so they do not call view.terminate() on an exited shell.
applyAppearance resets SwiftTerm colours, which clears its attribute caches and redraws (comment lines 43-44), so it is guarded to run only on a change.
platform_assumptions: SwiftTerm LocalProcessTerminalView (forkpty on macOS); a Windows port needs ConPTY and a Windows shell (PowerShell, cmd, Git Bash).
POSIX login-shell conventions: argv[0] prefixed with "-", flags "-l", "-i", "-c", and 'exec <shell> -l' after a command.
Darwin sysctl kinfo_proc to read the terminal's foreground process group; Windows has no process-group foreground concept and needs another test (e.g. ConPTY child process tree).
AppKit NSRect, NSColor(white:alpha:), NSString.lastPathComponent.
optionAsMetaKey = true (Option key sends Meta); the Windows analogue is Alt.
persisted_fields: None. Sessions and selection are not saved.
ui_elements: Initial terminal view frame 640 x 240.
Dark: background NSColor(white: 0.08, alpha: 1), foreground NSColor(white: 0.9, alpha: 1). Light: background NSColor(white: 0.985, alpha: 1), foreground NSColor(white: 0.12, alpha: 1).

Caret colour Chrome.accentNSColor; selection background accent.withAlphaComponent(0.3). Both are set inside applyAppearance AFTER `guard appliedDark != isDark else { return }` (line 48), so a change of the theme's accent while dark/light stays the same never reaches an open session's caret or selection; only a light/dark flip (or a new/restarted session, whose appliedDark starts nil) re-reads Chrome.accentNSColor.

Default tab title "Terminal N" where N = sessions(for: threadID).count + 1 at open time (lines 120-121: `let number = sessions(for: threadID).count + 1` and `title ?? "Terminal \(number)"`). There is no running counter, so numbers repeat after a close: with "Terminal 1" and "Terminal 2" open, closing "Terminal 1" and opening a new one gives a second "Terminal 2". Parity keeps this; a monotonically increasing counter would diverge.
feature_notes: Environment: LoginEnvironment.current plus TERM="xterm-256color", COLORTERM="truecolor", TERM_PROGRAM="Droppy Code", DROPPY_CODE_PROJECT_ROOT=<directory>; passed as "KEY=VALUE" strings.

execName is "-" + last path component of the shell; with no command args are []; with a command args are ["-l", "-i", "-c", "<command>; exec <shell> -l"] so the tab drops into an interactive login shell after the script.
foregroundJobIsTheShell returns false for pid <= 0 or a failed sysctl; true when e_tpgid == e_pgid.

processTerminated arrives from SwiftTerm and hops to the main actor to call processEnded() (isRunning = false). The other three delegate callbacks are empty (terminal title changes and cwd updates are ignored).
selected(for:): the session whose id equals selection[threadID], else the last session.
open: appends and selects the new session. run(script) opens with title script.name and command script.command.
ensureTerminal opens a default session only if the thread has none.

restart: terminate old (no-op if already exited), create a fresh TerminalSession with same threadID, directory and title and command nil (a script tab restarts as a plain shell), replace it at the same index (append if not found), select it. Because it constructs a new TerminalSession, TerminalFont.preferred() runs again and the new view's appliedDark starts nil, so font and colours are re-derived at that moment.
close: terminate, remove, and if it was selected select the thread's last remaining session (nil if none).
closeAll(for:) terminates each and removes the thread's entries; terminateAll terminates every session without removing them.

B1->B2: one line changed in TerminalSession.init: view.font = NSFont.monospacedSystemFont(ofSize: 12, weight: .regular) became view.font = TerminalFont.preferred() (the new TerminalFont.swift; still 12 pt monospaced system font as last fallback).
unresolved_questions: LoginEnvironment.userShell() and LoginEnvironment.current are defined elsewhere; the Windows shell choice must follow that file's port.

files.purpose: TourView.swift is the welcome tour card, credited in its header as a port of TourKit by Ram Patra (MIT, see THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md): a floating glass card with a 16:10 artwork section carrying a page indicator and back/close circle buttons, and a bottom panel with a bold title, a centred description and a prominent Continue/Done button. It defines the TourPage value type, the paging logic (advance, goBack, clamped initial index, last page finish chain onFinish then onClose then dismiss) and TourPageIndicator, a row of capsules with the current one widened.

files.purpose: TourWindowController is the @MainActor singleton that presents the welcome tour in its own borderless, transparent, floating NSWindow, centred over the visible main window titled "Droppy Code" (or the screen). Before showing it measures every page's bottom panel with an off-screen NSHostingView of TourBottomPanelSizingView and fixes the card height to image height plus the tallest panel, turning off the hosting view's sizing options so the window never grows or shrinks between pages; it re-fronts an existing tour instead of opening a second.

Sizing view mirrors TourView's bottom panel text only: Spacer(minLength: 12), title .system(size: 28, weight: .bold), description .body with top padding 6, Spacer(minLength: 12), then a plain Text of the button title in .system(.title3, weight: .semibold) in a 220 x 42 frame (not a Button, no .glassProminent style); padding horizontal 32, top 12, bottom 24; measured at .frame(width: width) via NSHostingView.layoutSubtreeIfNeeded() and fittingSize.height.

onFinish passed to TourView runs the caller's onFinish if given else the caller's onClose, then dismiss (close()). onClose runs the caller's onClose then dismiss.

hosting.sizingOptions = [] so the window keeps the computed size (comment lines 70-72 say the default resized the window per page).

close(): window?.close(), then nil both references. The WindowDelegate (lines 145-149) only forwards windowWillClose to the closure built at lines 103-106, which does `self?.window = nil; self?.windowDelegate = nil` and nothing else: it does NOT call the caller's onClose or onFinish. The caller's callbacks run only through TourView's Done/Continue (advance on the last page) and checkmark buttons; if the tour window closes any other way, neither callback runs.
initialPageIndex is not exposed by present(); the tour always starts on page 0.

B1->B2: one font change in TourBottomPanelSizingView: the button text .system(size: 15, weight: .semibold) became .system(.title3, weight: .semibold), the same font TourView.swift's primaryActionButton label now uses. Only the fonts are shown to match: the sizing view measures a bare `Text(verbatim: buttonTitle).font(.system(.title3, weight: .semibold)).frame(width: 220, height: 42)` (lines 178-180), while TourView renders that label inside `Button(action: advance) { ... }.buttonStyle(.glassProminent).keyboardShortcut(.defaultAction)` (TourView.swift lines 204-211). Any chrome the .glassProminent style draws around the 220 x 42 label is not measured, so the code does not show that the measured panel height includes the button bezel.

It reports its wanted content height to the placer, and its top strip is a drag handle carrying a 'Usage' title capsule with provider icons on the left and a dismiss circle button on the right.

files.purpose: UsagePanel is the body of the composer's usage popover (360 points wide) and of the floating usage panel: the context-window line with used/total tokens and a percentage over a UsageBar, then the provider's PlanLimitsView and CreditsView. When a Hydra pair sends its heads out on a different provider it stacks two sections headed 'Lead · <name>' and 'Heads · <name>'; on appear it refreshes limits and credits for each shown provider, and it owns the compact token formatter (k, M, B).

With heads: Lead section with needsDivider = showsContext; Heads section with needsDivider = showsContext || lead showsLimits || lead showsCredits. A section with neither limits nor credits renders nothing; inside a section a divider sits between limits and credits when both show.

tokens(): >= 1_000_000_000 -> value/1e9 with "B"; >= 1_000_000 -> "M"; >= 1_000 -> "k"; else the plain integer. compact uses String(format: "%.1f") and drops a trailing ".0" (1500 -> "1.5k", 200000 -> "200k"; 999_950 formats as "1000k" because the threshold is checked before rounding).

files.purpose: UsageViews.swift holds the shared usage building blocks used by both the composer's usage popover and Settings, Providers: PlanLimitsView (plan header, one LimitRow per rolling window, banked resets and a login or problem note), CreditsView (remaining pay-as-you-go balance with a Top up link), and the thin UsageBar capsule. It also implements the banked-reset flow for Codex reset credits and Z.ai reset cards: a count header, a row per reset with a Use reset -> Cancel / Reset now confirmation, a spinner while the registry spends it, and an outcome or error line that clears after 4 seconds.

Flow: Use reset -> phase .confirming(id); Cancel -> .idle; Reset now -> spend() (lines 293-307): `phase = .applying(row.id)`, then `settle?.cancel()` (cancels the previous Task, e.g. one still in its 4-second sleep), then `settle = Task { ... }` that awaits consumeResetCredit(provider, row.credit?.id) and sets `phase = .done(outcome)` or `.failed(error.localizedDescription)` with no cancellation check, then `try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(4))`, and only the reset to `.idle` is guarded by `guard !Task.isCancelled else { return }`. A cancelled task whose request is still pending would still write .done/.failed when it returns; the UI makes that overlap hard to reach because "Use reset" is `.disabled(isApplying)` while any row is .applying and "Reset now" only shows in .confirming. onDisappear cancels settle.
The refresh of limits is the caller's job; PlanLimitsView only renders (comment line 6).
